newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt sees 5 pct GDP growth in 1997-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt sees 5 pct GDP growth in 1997-report.

text.p: The Brazilian government forecasts five percent economic growth in 1997 with gross domestic product (GDP) reaching 800 billion reais ($800 billion), a newspaper said.
Government economic officials said GDP would grow a maximum of 3 percent this year and 5 percent next year, according to Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper.

The economic officials said the pursuit of economic growth would bring with it a further deficit in the trade balance of around $5 billion in 1997, compared with this year's gap of $2-3 billion, Folha de Sao Paulo said.
The government plans to finance the trade deficit with foreign investment and part of its $59.6 billion in foreign reserves.
The governent predicts a reduction in the public sector deficit to 2-2.5 percent of GDP in 1997 from 3.5 percent of GDP this year.
Interest rates are expected to fall from 24 percent a year this year to between 15 and 20 percent next year.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
